transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-03-05
Time: 15:00 PT / 18:00 ET
Duration: ~39 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Myers (Redwood AE), Priya Singh (Redwood SE), Carlos Ramirez (Nova Head of ML), Maya Patel (Nova Cloud Architect), Evan Li (Nova Procurement)

Summary (auto):
Quick check-in ahead of renewal to confirm capacity needs, region expansion to EU, and contract extension timing. Discussed performance benchmarks, dedicated vs. hybrid routing, and procurement timelines.

Topics:
- Dedicated capacity upgrade sizing (8xA100 -> 16xA100 equiv)
- Additional region (EU-west) for data residency and lower latency
- Contract length and pricing for 12-month extension
- Security/compliance artifacts for procurement and on-prem/VPC options
- Scheduling a benchmark run with Nova data

Action items (captured):
- Jordan to send updated quote + region pricing
- Priya to share SOC2/ISO & VPC network diagram
- Carlos/Priya to agree benchmark dataset and windows
- Evan to confirm PO timeline

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan: okay everybody thanks for joining, um, we wanted to keep this pretty short just a renewal and expansion check in, uh, Jordan from Redwood here and with me is Priya, our solutions engineer.
[00:12] Priya: hey all, hi, thanks for making time.
[00:15] Carlos: yeah thanks, appreciate it. We, we put this on because we're approaching the end of our committed period and there's some internal asks to, um, increase capacity and also have EU presence.
[00:27] Jordan: totally, and congrats on the season of growth—happy to help. Quick one: can you confirm current usage shape? we have your telemetry showing spikes at peak retail hours, right?
[00:40] Carlos: yep, right now we're about 120k tokens peak per minute, average latencies around 180–200ms with the hosted flow, but p90 jumps during promos. The dedicated pool's been great but we're hitting throttles in two regions.
[00:55] Maya: and just to add, latency to EU customers is not great, we see a 60–90ms extra RTT to us-east region. So EU region would be high priority.
[01:08] Priya: ok that helps. So you're currently on a dedicated 8 GPU equivalent commit, is that right?
[01:14] Carlos: correct, 8x A100 equiv.
[01:17] Jordan: and the ask is scale to 16? what's the target throughput you want to support for Black Friday style spikes or promotional windows?
[01:26] Carlos: we'd like to design for 2x current peak so roughly 240k tokens/min sustained for short windows, maybe 10–20 minutes with burst to 400k. That maps to roughly 16x A100 equiv from our internal calc.
[01:40] Priya: makes sense. For that footprint we generally recommend dedicated pool of 16 with autoscaling burst to 20 for short windows; also consider prefix caching and aggressive batching in those windows. That will keep unit cost down and maintain p95 latency.
[01:54] Maya: question — for the EU region, do you deploy a separate dedicated pool or can we route EU traffic to the same pool using regional edge routing? We want data residency in EU so I think separate region is required.
[02:07] Priya: yes, if you need residency and isolation we recommend a separate dedicated pool in eu-west region; we can set up smart routing so EU hits EU pool and fallback to global only if capacity constrained, but fallback policies can be off if you want strict locality.
[02:22] Carlos: and is there an additional start-up fee for a second region? we saw line items before for dedicated setup.
[02:30] Jordan: typically there is a small provisioning fee the first time for a new region (mostly operational), we'll include that in the quote. For committed capacity pricing it's additive — meaning you commit to X capacity in each region and we give volume discounts across the contract.
[02:44] Evan: from procurement side — what's the impact on contract term? if we add another region and increase capacity, do we need to sign a new PO right away or can we amend the existing renewal to cover the expansion?
[02:55] Jordan: we can do either. Common approach is extend current contract for 12 months with an amendment that adds the EU region and increased commit; that avoids churn. We'll provide options: amendment vs separate SOW — we'll put both in the quote.
[03:09] Maya: timeline wise, we need EU up before May 1st for a new product launch. Is that feasible?
[03:16] Priya: yes, we can provision and validate within 4–6 weeks typically for a dedicated pool plus validation and test runs — depends on final sizing and procurement timing.
[03:26] Carlos: ok good. Can we also do a bench with our test corpus to validate p95/p99 latencies and cost per token?
[03:33] Priya: absolutely. We usually schedule a 2-hour benchmarking window where we push your test set and measure latency, throughput, and token cost with the proposed config. We'll need a secure upload link for the dataset and a contact on your side.
[03:46] Carlos: I can own that, I'll share a sanitized dataset and credentials.
[03:50] Jordan: perfect. Evan, any concerns from procurement on renewal length?
[03:54] Evan: yeah the team prefers a 12-month renewal but we'd like pricing protections and an option to increase capacity mid-term without renegotiating pricing tiers. Also want to understand termination and refund for unused commit during migration windows.
[04:08] Jordan: we can provide a 12-month fixed pricing table with tiered commit breakpoints and an agreed-upon mid-term scale clause — basically ability to add capacity at the same rate card up to X% bump, and an early termination shortfall schedule. We'll include language for pro-rata refunds for any capacity we cannot provision because of force majeure or some migration issue.
[04:29] Evan: good — procurement wants SOC2 type 2, ISO27001 and evidence of encryption at rest and in transit; also network diagrams for the VPC peering if we go private.
[04:41] Priya: we'll send our security pack — SOC2 Type II, ISO27k certs, pen test summary. For VPC we provide a recommended architecture, sample VPC peering configs and KMS/HSM integration notes.
[04:54] Maya: for internal compliance we also need to know about data retention and logs — specifically how long KV caches are retained and if logs include PII in request traces.
[05:03] Priya: by default we don't persist KV cache across customers; caching is per-prefix and you can configure TTLs. Audit logs show request/response hashes but we redacted PII by default; if you enable full logging you can manage retention policies — we'll share the exact fields and retention options.
[05:20] Carlos: great. A quick note on performance: during our holiday promo we saw p95 jump to 600ms with the hosted fallback; with dedicated it was usually 220ms. Will doubling capacity get p95 down below 250ms under load?
[05:32] Priya: with the recommended 16 commit and aggressive prefex cache and batching tuning, we should see p95 around 200–250ms for your model and workloads. The benchmark will confirm.
[05:43] Jordan: I'm going to capture two pricing scenarios — 12-month commit for 16 GPUs and a 24-month extended with deeper discounts. Do you have preference?
[05:52] Evan: procurement leans to 12 months but are open to 24 if price delta is compelling. The team also asked for a clause to align renewal dates across regions so we don't have staggered renewals.
[06:04] Jordan: we can align region contracts on a single master term and have region-specific SKUs; we'll put that option in the quote.
[06:12] Carlos: any risks we should know about for EU region, e.g., model licensing, perf differences, or additional SOC/regulatory checks?
[06:20] Priya: performance differences are usually negligible with same GPU types; main gaps are network and cold-start warmup. For licensing we can host models that you're running if they have allowable EEA deployment; otherwise we have curated open models or verified partners. We'll include the list of supported model images for EU region.
[06:36] Maya: and what about hybrid routing during rollout? can we send a percentage of traffic to EU pool while keeping the rest to US until all tests pass?
[06:45] Priya: yes, Redwood supports canary routing and percentage splits. You can also configure fallback to global pool if EU capacity is exhausted, but for strict residency we leave fallback off.
[06:56] Evan: procurement also asked if we can get an SLA addendum for dedicated pools — 99.95 or similar.
[07:02] Jordan: dedicated customers commonly get 99.9 to 99.95 depending on commit and monitoring add-ons. We'll quote the SLA tiers and associated credits.
[07:11] Carlos: sounds good. Let's talk schedule — what's the earliest we could get the benchmark?
[07:15] Priya: if you send the dataset by Monday we'll propose two slots next Wednesday and Friday for a 2-hour window.
[07:22] Carlos: I'll aim for Monday.
[07:23] Jordan: ok great. Quick recap then: Jordan will send an updated quote with both amendment and SOW options, include commit options for 12 vs 24 months, region provisioning fee, and SLA tiers. Priya will share security artifacts and sample VPC diagrams. Carlos will provide sanitized test dataset. Evan will confirm procurement timing. We'll target EU region live by May 1st pending PO and benchmarks.
[07:45] Maya: that works, thanks everyone.
[07:48] Jordan: thanks all, we'll follow up via email and update the CRM. Links: quote draft (https://redwood.app/quote/CRM-68294), security pack link (share after call), benchmark doc (internal).
[07:58] Speaker 1: thanks bye.

End of transcript.
